facts.statement: Aragosaurus was a sauropod dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous period in Galve, Teruel, Spain.
facts.quote: Aragosaurus (meaning "Aragon lizard") was a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of Galve, province of Teruel, in the autonomous territory of Aragón, Spain.

facts.statement: Aragosaurus was a large, quadrupedal herbivore that lived during the early Berriasian, approximately 145 to 140 million years ago.
facts.quote: Aragosaurus was a large, quadrupedal plant-eating (herbivorous) dinosaur, which lived during the early Berriasian, about 145-140 million years ago.

facts.statement: Aragosaurus reached a length of about 18 meters and weighed approximately 25 tonnes.
facts.quote: It was about 18 m in length and about 25 tonnes in weight.

facts.statement: Aragosaurus had large, wide teeth adapted for slicing leaves and branches from tall conifer trees.
facts.quote: The teeth were large and wide, and would have been useful for slicing through the leaves and branches of tall conifer trees.

facts.statement: Aragosaurus ischiaticus is the only known species of the extinct sauropod genus Aragosaurus, a macronarian that lived in Europe approximately 136 million years ago during the Hauterivian.
facts.quote: Aragosaurus ischiaticus ("lagarto de Aragón con gran isquion") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Aragosaurus de dinosaurio saurópodo macronario que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 136 millones de años, en el Hauteriviense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: Aragosaurus was a heavy herbivore nearly 18 meters long and weighing about 20 tonnes, living in environments near the coast of the Tethys Sea.
facts.quote: Aragosaurus fue un pesado herbívoro de casi 18 metros de longitud y aproximadamente 20 toneladas de peso, que vivió en los ambientes cercanos a la costa del mar de Tetis.

facts.statement: Related to Camarasaurus, Aragosaurus had spatulate teeth ornamented with longitudinal grooves.
facts.quote: Emparentado con el camarasaurio, el aragosaurio dispone de dientes con forma espatulada, ornamentados por surcos longitudinales.

facts.statement: The first caudal vertebrae of Aragosaurus were robust with widened neural spines, likely serving as anchor points for ligaments that consolidated the upper region of the tail base.
facts.quote: Las primeras vértebras caudales son robustas y presentan ensanchamientos en las espinas neurales que, se supone, servían para el anclaje de los ligamentos que consolidan la región superior de la base de la cola.

facts.statement: Like its relative Camarasaurus, Aragosaurus had large holes in its cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Además, como su pariente el camarasaurio, presentaba grandes huecos en las vértebras cervicales.

facts.statement: The species name A. ischiaticus refers to the robust pelvis, specifically the large development of the pubic process of the ischium and the mace-like expansion of the ischiatic process.
facts.quote: La única especie debe su nombre (A. ischiaticus) al robustecimiento de la cadera que se refleja principalmente en el gran desarrollo del proceso púbico del isquion y la expansión mazuda del proceso isquiático.

facts.statement: Aragosaurus had forelimbs shorter than its hind limbs, though not as drastically short as is common in other camarasaurids.
facts.quote: Los brazos de Aragosaurus son más cortos que los miembros posteriores, aunque no tanto como es común en los camarasáuridos.

facts.statement: The femur of Aragosaurus could reach a length of 1.4 meters.
facts.quote: El fémur del aragosaurio puede alcanzar la longitud de 1,4 metro.

facts.statement: The type species A. ischiaticus was discovered by José María Herrero Marzo in 1958.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, A. ischiaticus, fue descubierta por José María Herrero Marzo en 1958.

facts.statement: Aragosaurus was finally described by Sanz, Buscalioni, Casanovas, and Santafé in 1987 from the El Castellar Formation in Galve, Teruel, Spain.
facts.quote: descrita finalmente por Sanz, Buscalioni, Casanovas y Santafé en 1987 en la Formación El Castellar, en Galve, Teruel, España.

facts.statement: The genus Aragosaurus and the species A. ischiaticus were named by Sanz et al. in 1987.
facts.quote: genus: Aragosaurus genus_authority: Sanz et al., 1987 species: Aragosaurus ischiaticus species_authority: Sanz et al., 1987

facts.statement: Aragosaurus is classified within the unranked family Macronaria.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Macronaria

facts.statement: The discovery of Aragosaurus supported the theory that all continents were once united in Pangea millions of years ago.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de este dinosaurio apoyó la teoría de que hace millones de años todos los continentes estaban unidos en uno solo (Pangea).

facts.statement: Close relatives of Aragosaurus lived in nearby areas like modern-day Portugal, while others lived in distant regions such as North America or East Africa.
facts.quote: Parientes cercanos al Aragosaurus vivían en zonas cercanas, como el actual Portugal, pero otros vivían en zonas lejanas como América del Norte o el este de África.

facts.statement: Original Aragosaurus fossils are exhibited at the Paleontological Museum of Galve and in Dinópolis-Legendark.
facts.quote: Los fósiles originales de Aragosaurus se encuentran expuestos en el Museo Paleontológico de Galve y en Dinópolis-Legendark.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range for Aragosaurus as Kimmeridgian to Tithonian, from 154.8 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Aragosaurus possessed a long neck, a long powerful tail, a small head, and a bulky body typical of sauropods.
rejected.quote: Like other sauropods, it had a long neck, a long powerful tail, a small head and a bulky body.
